 Mobile Google confirms native app lock won't come to older Android versions
 App lock needs more than a Play system update. Hillary Keverenge • Nov 20, 2026 — 1:17 AM ET 
 • • Pankil Shah / Android Authority Add Android Authority on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover TL;DR 
 Google has confirmed that Android’s native app lock cannot be backported to older Android versions via Play System updates.
 The current implementation depends on new APIs in the core Android platform.
 Users will need an Android OS update, not a Google Play System update, to get Google’s current implementation of App Lock.
 Between Samsung introducing native app lock in One UI 9.5 this week and Google restoring the feature in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3 last month, it’s been a good few weeks for Android users who value their privacy. And with Google increasingly delivering Android features outside of major OS updates , some users are wondering whether their phones could get native app locking without upgrading to the latest version of Android.
 Unfortunately, this isn’t one of those features.
 In response to a question on Reddit about bringing App Lock to older Android versions through Google Play system updates, Google’s Mishaal Rahman clarified:
 Because app lock utilizes new APIs in the core Android platform, the current implementation can’t be backported to previous Android versions via Google Play system updates. 
 Google Play system updates allow Google to update certain parts of Android without requiring phone manufacturers to issue a full software update. However, not every part of the operating system can be updated this way, and the underlying changes needed for App Lock fall outside that scope.
 That’s understandable considering how deeply the feature integrates with Android. Beyond requiring a fingerprint, PIN, pattern, or password to open protected apps, App Lock hides notification content, removes home screen widgets and shortcuts, obscures app previews in the Recents menu, and hides direct sharing targets from protected apps.
 The good news is that Google has now provided a release window. In the same Reddit thread, Rahman revealed that the product team plans to release App Lock with Android 17 QPR3 in the first quarter of 2027.
 This doesn’t necessarily mean phones running older versions of Android will never get native app locking. Manufacturers can develop their own implementations, as some like Xiaomi have already done for years. But those hoping Google could deliver its current implementation through a simple Google Play system update shouldn’t count on it.
